problem: PanoGen generates panoramic training environments with a general-purpose text-to-image diffusion model that is agnostic to VLN/Matterport3D style, so generated scenes have a domain gap and lose VLN-specific details. Training environments for VLN (61 MP3D houses) remain scarce.
motivation: Data scarcity limits VLN generalization to unseen environments, and manual collection of new 3D scans is costly. Generative augmentation is cheap, but only useful if the generated images match the simulator's distribution and remain semantically aligned with instructions.
key_idea: Adapt a pre-trained Stable Diffusion (text encoder + U-Net attention) to the MP3D VLN domain with LoRA on BLIP-2-captioned MP3D view images, then use it for masked center-crop inpainting or recursive outpainting to generate panoramas that replace original observations during VLN training.
insight: Domain adaptation of the generator via LoRA reduces FID vs PanoGen (Matterport3D 40.754 -> 32.908 inpainting / 38.081 outpainting) and improves R2R SPL (val unseen 59.54 -> 64.88), showing domain-matched generated data matters more than generic world knowledge. Ablations show the replacement ratio (best SR at 50%), peripheral masking with a preserved center (PRM best SR/SPL among masking strategies), and number of views for adaptation (6,500 best) all matter; rank 64 was best. On REVERIE the gains are small and it still trails DUET/AZHP, suggesting random replacement loses fine object cues.
method: VLN-specific caption data: split 7,705 R2R training panoramas into 36 sub-views each (12 headings x 3 elevations, 30° apart), giving 277,380 images, captioned by BLIP-2-FlanT5-xxL with prompt 'a photo of'.

LoRA domain adaptation: add low-rank ΔW=BA (rank 64) to the CLIP text encoder and U-Net attention layers of Stable Diffusion v2.1 (and its inpainting model), trained with the standard LDM noise-prediction loss L_da while all other weights are frozen (lr 1e-7, batch 8, 40k iterations).
Masked image inpainting setting: keep a central 128x128 crop of a sub-view, mask the periphery (PRM), and inpaint guided by the caption to create novel scenes that keep central content.

Recursive image outpainting setting: generate one sub-view from its caption, then shift the window right/down/up with 50% overlap and outpaint neighbouring sub-views using their captions to form a coherent panorama (following PanoGen).

Agent training with DUET: pre-train with MLM, MRM and SAP on original plus generated environments; fine-tune with pseudo-interactive demonstrator loss while randomly replacing p% of trajectory viewpoint observations with generated panoramas (best p=0.5).

setting.backbone: DUET (dual-scale graph transformer) agent trained with augmented data; generator is Stable Diffusion v2.1 + LoRA (rank 64); captions by BLIP-2-FlanT5-xxL
setting.training_data: MP3D R2R/R4R/CVDN/REVERIE training environments; plus generated panoramas from the LoRA-adapted generator (fine-tuned on 277,380 BLIP-2 captioned MP3D sub-views from 7,705 panoramas); generator itself pre-trained on web data (Stable Diffusion)
setting.observation: 36-view panoramic RGB at each node (topological graph), GPS position
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (move to neighboring node or stop)
setting.privileged: none at test time (pseudo interactive demonstrator uses env graph only during training)

numbers_note: Text and tables are inconsistent in places: the prose reports R2R test SR 73.47/SPL 62.05 (inpainting) and val-unseen SR 74.67 (outpainting), and the abstract cites a 2.44% test-leaderboard SR gain, which don't match Table 1. The CVDN GP is 6.13 in prose vs 6.38 in Table 2. Table values are used here.
results: PanoGen++ improves over PanoGen and DUET on R2R (val-unseen SR 75.12 / SPL 64.88 vs PanoGen 74.03 / 59.54 and DUET 72.00 / 60.00), and on R4R and CVDN it slightly beats PanoGen (R4R SR 48.41 vs 47.78, CVDN GP 6.38 vs 5.63). FID to Matterport3D is lowered from 40.754 to 32.908. On REVERIE it improves over PanoGen but remains below DUET and AZHP.
limitations: Generated panoramas show geometric inconsistencies at panorama edges, blur in some regions and non-uniform textures, and BLIP-2 captions occasionally misidentify structures.
Random replacement of observations loses fine-grained object cues, so gains on object-centric REVERIE are small and it trails DUET/AZHP.
Diversity is bounded by the quality and range of the MP3D image-text pairs used for adaptation; inconsistencies between reported numbers in text and tables.
